title: Let the database enforce the rules: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY
problem: schema.py creates the users, chats and chat_members tables with the right columns but no rules. Add the constraints described in the comments so that invalid data is rejected by the database itself, and make connect() turn on foreign-key enforcement.
requirements: chats.kind is required and is 'direct' or 'group'; a group chat must have a title
chat_members.chat_id and user_id are required and reference chats and users
Deleting a chat deletes its memberships; deleting a user who is still a member is refused
chat_members.role is required, defaults to 'member', and is one of 'owner', 'admin', 'member'
connect() enables foreign keys on the connection
expectedBehavior: Every invalid INSERT or DELETE in the tests raises sqlite3.IntegrityError; DELETE FROM chats WHERE id = 1 also removes that chat's memberships
edgeCases: NULL passes a CHECK unless the column is NOT NULL
A direct chat without a title is valid
Foreign keys are off in SQLite until enabled per connection
Deleting a parent row that is still referenced
hints: Conceptual: each rule maps to one constraint: required -> NOT NULL, unique -> UNIQUE, allowed values or a rule across columns -> CHECK, references -> REFERENCES with an ON DELETE action. SQLite also needs one PRAGMA per connection.
Specific: a CHECK passes when its expression is NULL, so pair it with NOT NULL. 'A group must have a title' compares two columns, so write it as a table-level CHECK after the columns.

Implementation: kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('direct', 'group')); CHECK (kind = 'direct' OR title IS NOT NULL); chat_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES chats(id) ON DELETE CASCADE; role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member' CHECK (role IN (...)); conn.execute('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON') in connect().
evaluation: Constraints have names where they're CHECKs
No validation code in Python: the schema does the work
